rv.q: And Jackman, in his element, has us rapt.
But despite sterling, intermittently touching performances from both actors, the play feels less convincing than those similar two-character dramas.
Both are eminently worth a visit.
Theater lovers with strong attention spans will leave awed by the acting, writing, and direction.
These are all talented performers, but they haven’t quite found their footing with this material.

cn.t: Ella Hickson's ambitious triptych of monologues earns praise for its skillful execution and emotional resonance, with Hugh Jackman leading a strong cast in Ian Rickson's stripped-down production at the intimate Minetta Lane Theatre.
